lesson.text: Quick memory: which notes sit on the lines of the treble stave? (E, G, B, D and F, from the bottom.) Today: reading a whole melody, its notes and its rhythm.
A melody has pitch (how high or low: where each note sits on the stave) and rhythm (how long: each note's value). Read both, note by note.
Note values: a semibreve lasts 4 beats, a dotted minim 3, a minim 2, a crotchet 1 and a quaver half a beat. A quaver on its own has a flag on its stem.
The time signature says how many beats are in each bar: 4/4 has 4, 3/4 has 3. Bar lines split the melody into bars, the way spaces split words.
Steps and leaps: from a line to the next space, or a space to the next line, is a step; skipping over lines or spaces is a leap. Spotting them helps you sing a tune before you hear it.
Worked example: E, G, G and A are crotchets, then B is a minim: 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 6 beats. E to G is a leap, G to G stays, and G to A and A to B are steps.
Read a new tune in four stages: clap its rhythm, say its letter names, sing it slowly, then play or sing it in time.
Try it in the world: find a tune written on a stave, in a songbook or in this School, clap its rhythm, then say its notes. Can you sing it before you hear it? Next: playing together.

exercises.hint: G sits on the second line; the notes step up from there.
exercises.explain: G on a line, A in the space above, B on the middle line: G A B.

exercises.prompt: How many beats do these notes last?
A quaver lasts half a beat.
exercises.hint: Two quavers fit into one crotchet beat.
exercises.explain: True: a quaver is half a beat, so two quavers make one beat.

exercises.prompt: Listen. Does this tune go up or down?
exercises.hint: Does each note sound higher or lower than the one before?
exercises.explain: C, D, E, F, G: each note is higher, so it goes up.

exercises.prompt: Listen. Which stave shows the tune you heard?
exercises.hint: Did the tune go up or down? Did a note come twice, and where?
exercises.explain: It went E, G, G, A, B: a leap up, the same note again, then steps up.

exercises.prompt: How many beats do these notes last?
exercises.hint: Quaver ½, crotchet 1, minim 2. Add them up.
exercises.explain: Two quavers make 1 beat, so 1 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 5 beats.

exercises.hint: They are all on lines. Every Green Bus Drives Fast.
exercises.explain: The five lines from the bottom: E G B D F.

exercises.prompt: In 3/4 time, how many crotchet beats fill each bar?
exercises.hint: Read the top number of the time signature.
exercises.explain: 3/4 means 3 crotchet beats in every bar.

exercises.prompt: Listen. The tune matches the notes on the stave.
exercises.hint: Follow the notes with your finger as you listen.
exercises.explain: True: you heard C, E, G, E, and the stave shows C, E, G, E.

exercises.prompt: How many beats do these notes last?
The time signature is 3/4. How many full bars do these notes fill?
exercises.hint: Add up the beats, then see how many 3s they make.

exercises.prompt: Listen, then look at the stave. Which note is different from what you heard?
exercises.hint: Follow each note as you listen. Where does the stave go somewhere else?
exercises.explain: You heard C, D, E, C, but the stave's 4th note is D.

exercises.prompt: Listen. Which stave shows the tune you heard?
exercises.hint: Listen for where it starts, and which notes come twice.
exercises.explain: G, then E twice, F, then D twice: the stave that starts on the second line.

exercises.prompt: Listen and look. How many beats does this melody last?
exercises.hint: Minim 2, crotchet 1, dotted minim 3. Add them up.

exercises.prompt: Which of these is a leap?
exercises.hint: A leap skips over a letter.
exercises.explain: E to G skips F, so it is a leap; the others go to the very next letter.

exercises.hint: They are all in the spaces: they spell a word.
exercises.explain: The four spaces from the bottom spell FACE: F A C E.
